comments.text: Hi. Great vid. Just wanted to confirm one thing. For ex. I currently have mediclaim policy with a co. And i want to stop with that and go with a new health insurance co. Which can provide better benefits and advantages, so if i port from existing one to a new one, will the premium increase in new co. & what are the things that can be carry forward and benefits of porting to new co.? Also what are the disadvantages of porting (if any)? Or we should get a fresh policy with new co.? Thanks
comments.author: @LaughLoveLifestyle

comments.text:
When you port to a new company, you get the benefits of the new company and also pay premium that new company is charging - it can higher/ lower or same.

Continuity benefits will be given in case of portability.

If portability is an option, don't go for a fresh policy.

For details on portability , pls refer the below detailed video on our channel

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQd0u2-_UF8

comments.text:
Hello madam...madam I have multiple questions, request you to answer these
1)if disease occurred after taking health insurance (like Myasthenia Gravis)....is it compulsory to inform insurance company ?
2) If yes than what could be consequence of not informing ? 
3) Suppose I hide disease A which occurred after taking health plan and claim occurred for disease B than can company rejects claim?
4)I heard as per regulatory guideline 
if I continue to renew health plan for continues 7 claim free years than company cant refuse claim in any case. Is it true? Is there any regulatory guidelines in this matter? What is that clause?
comments.author: @thesniper2807

comments.text:
1. If the disease is not a PED and occured after buying the policy, then it is not necessary to inform the insurance company.

2. No effect on the policy.

3. At the time of claim, you should be having a first consultation paper when this disease was diagnosed as a proof that this was not a PED.

4. Yes, it is called moratorium period that company can't reject claim if policy has been running straight for 8 years.(T&C apply)
